_why: Role track for CONVENTIONAL MACHINING -- centre lathe, vertical milling, radial drill, boring and shaping, all by hand. fam_machining stays the generic machining interview bound at ISCO unit 7223; this pack binds the NCO conventional-machining occupations directly (job_domain specificity 50 beats unit 40), so a manual machinist gets manual depth and every other machining worker is untouched. It is the manual-side rival qp_cnc_turning and qp_vmc_milling never had: a man who says only 'khraad' is speaking the truth for both trades, and this pack is what makes his half of that word answerable.
_scope: NO CONTROLLER, NO PROGRAM, AND THAT IS THE ROLE. Every other machining pack in the corpus asks controller_brand and programming_level; a conventional machinist has neither, and asking him would burn two of eight base asks to record two 'Pata nahi' answers. What replaces them is what the ratified sheet actually prints for this trade: the OPERATIONS he performs by hand, the CAPACITY of the machine he stands at, and the rung he calls himself. machining_level is asked rather than inferred because the reference headline reads 'Conventional Machinist -- Skilled': role-form-descriptor.ts states that the ladder is PRINTED, NOT INFERRED, so the rung has to be a fact the worker taps.
_depth: THE TIER GATE IS machining_experience, asked FIRST, and conventional-machinist.role.ts already names it as this role's tenureQuestionKey. It cannot be experience_years from qp_universal: phase order runs occupation_specific BEFORE universal_tail, so the universal answer does not exist yet when these items are selected. Its options carry value_number ONLY. pack-registry.service.ts resolves valueText ?? valueNumber ?? valueBool, so adding a value_text would make the answer a STRING; every gte below would then compare a string to a number, compare() returns null, and the predicate is false forever. A permanently-false ask_if is a question that is never asked, silently -- the #776 defect that sat in qp_welding for the life of the pack. The predicate shape is {op, left:{field}, right:{const}} for exactly the same reason: {op, args:[...]} parses and evaluates to nothing.
_budget: MAX_ENGINE_ASKS is 28 and qp_universal spends 8. Tier 0 is 8 items (16 total), tier 1 adds 3 (19), tier 2 adds 4 (23), leaving 5 asks of headroom. The three fresher items are gated on machining_experience <= 0 and a senior never sees them; a fresher skips tiers 1 and 2 entirely, so his worst case is 16 + 3 = 19. The tiers are mutually exclusive by construction, which is why the fresher branch costs the senior nothing.
_sheet: SECTION B IS READ OFF THE RATIFIED REFERENCE SHEET (Ram Naresh Gupta, Conventional Machinist -- Skilled, 12 yrs), not invented. Its eight rows are Machines, Materials, Operations, Measuring instruments, Drawings, Turning capacity, Tolerance held and Sector worked, and every one has a question here that fills it. THE OPERATIONS ITEM CARRIES NINE CHIPS, one more than this corpus likes, and the page is the reason: it prints eight ticks -- Turning & facing, Screw cutting, Knurling, Milling & slotting, Drilling & reaming, Boring, Tapping, Marking & scribing -- and a chip list short of eight is a row that cannot reproduce the sheet. The ninth is the none-of-above escape a helper needs. Turning capacity and tolerance are BANDED single-selects rather than free numbers: the sheet prints 'Up to 400 mm dia, 1500 mm bed' and '+/-0.05 mm', which are bands, and a banded chip keeps a low-literacy worker tapping instead of typing while avoiding the answer_type 'number' path that has no Flutter widget. FOUR ITEMS ARE CAPTURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT PRINTED -- machining_level feeds the headline rung rather than a capability row, and setting_operation, tool_grinding and advanced_work are real matching data for which the ratified page has no row. Inventing rows for them is what the guide's section 8 forbids.
review_note: Drafted for owner review (Prakash). Shop-floor vocabulary NOT yet corrected by a practising conventional machinist -- see docs/registers/trade-content-ratification.md.
_fresher: Guideline section 11 #1: a fresher's Zone 4 is training, trade test, machines used in the ITI workshop and project work, and the History heading never renders empty. These three items are the ask half; resume-fresher-rows.ts, fed by this role's descriptor, is the render half. The keys iti_workshop_machines and trade_test_status are read LITERALLY by that file and may never be renamed.
